notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.6.12.2 prints ENTER, language-name-1, an optional routine-name-1 and a separator period ("language-name-1 [ routine-name-1 ] ."), and §1985:IV.2.1.6 makes that period part of the format: "The separator period, when used in the formats, has the status of a required word." Implemented at 85: enterStatement is `ENTER enterOperand enterOperand?` with enterOperand one word token (IDENTIFIER, or LINKAGE), StatementBinder.BindStatementCore binds it as a no-op, and VersionConformancePass.VisitEnterStatement is the edition arm, refusing the statement from COBOL-2002 (COBOL0902), so 1985 alone accepts it. Probed at --std 85: ENTER COBOL., ENTER FORTRAN SUB1., ENTER LINKAGE. and lower case compile and run; ENTER with no operand, with a literal and with three words is refused. Not implemented, two arms. (1) The period: enterStatement is an ordinary statement alternative with no period of its own, so ENTER COBOL followed by another statement in the same sentence compiles. (2) Routine-name-1 as a COBOL word: the slot takes only an IDENTIFIER token and does not offer the gated-word reading the definition slots have, so a routine-name spelled as a word a later edition makes a verb (FREE, UNLOCK, RESUME, ALLOCATE, VALIDATE, RAISE, INVOKE, GOBACK; none is a 1985 reserved word, §1985:VI.6.12.3 SR2 "Routine-name-1 is a COBOL word") is read as the next statement and the sentence is refused at its period; the same word as language-name-1 is accepted, because there the error token is the word itself and NoteGatedOffender frees it. Arm (2) follows from arm (1): with the period required after the operands, the word could not begin another statement. Both arms stand while ENTER with another language-name is accepted at 85; the owner question recorded on 1985-SR-VI.6.12.3-1 may remove that acceptance. The statement is inert, so neither arm changes what a program computes. The witness is ENTER COBOL. between two DISPLAY sentences.

next.reason: 1985: "ENTER language-name-1 [ routine-name-1 ] ."; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the ENTER statement; the only wording match is CRT status for the operator's enter key.". No 2023 clause carries the ENTER statement. The wording candidate concerns CRT status after pressing the enter key, a different subject, so 2023 lacks the statement.
